blocks.title: A timeline in the side panel
blocks.description: A timeline, clips, colour and sound — the upstream FilmCraft editor running inside Astravia, on your own machine, with the project you opened in the workspace.

showcase.user_prompt: Trim to 20 s, warm the opening.
showcase.assistant_reply: Trimmed to 20 s, first shot warmed. Saved, not rendered.

items.title: The real editor
items.description: The tab runs the official FilmCraft web build byte for byte. Upstream's wasm and JavaScript are not patched; only two thin files of ours are added around them.

items.title: Open and render through the workspace
items.description: Opening uses the file selected in the Explorer, and whatever the editor hands back is written through Astravia instead of a downloads folder.

items.title: It retries rendering instead of giving up
items.description: If WebGPU is unavailable the tab reloads the page with upstream's own WebGL flag, then software, before it reports a failure.

items.title: A cut, reviewed before rendering
items.description: Clips are trimmed on the timeline, the playhead is moved and the frame is captured, so a cut is judged on a real frame instead of being discovered after a render.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: About 15 MB of editor files arrive on first open and are reused offline after that.

items.title: Open it from the composer
items.description: Press / or the first button left of the composer and pick FilmCraft from the plugin list. Its tab opens with it, and a toggle appears in the input bar. Turning the toggle off drops that context — it does not close the document you are editing.

items.title: Select a project, then open it
items.description: File → Open inside the editor takes the file selected in Astravia rather than a system dialog.

items.title: Render back through the workspace
items.description: Output travels the same bridge as a save, so it lands where you chose.

blocks.content: Upstream reloads itself with a flag when it has to drop from WebGPU to WebGL; the tab survives that reload and reports which backend is active in the status line.
Interface language: the editor itself is English only — upstream ships no other language. The tab shell and this page follow your Astravia language.

It trims on the timeline and moves the playhead the way you would. A cut is reported only after the frame at the new in-point has been captured — nothing is rendered to find out whether the cut is right.
